q-95012.name: Question 1
q-95012.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-95012.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 9{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & 7{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=2 \\ 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ 9{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-7 \\ 7{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-\frac{7}{6}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\frac{13}{2} & -13 \\ 0 & \frac{13}{6} & \frac{13}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=2 \\ -\frac{13}{2}{x}_{2}=-13 \\ \frac{13}{6}{x}_{2}=\frac{13}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second, third and fourth equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+5\cdot 2 & =4 \\ 6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.$

q-95021.name: Question 2
q-95021.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-95021.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ 9{x}_{2}=3 \\ -6{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2\cdot \frac{1}{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{1} & =1-\frac{2}{3} \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}.$

q-95027.name: Question 3
q-95027.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1-3{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(-3t+{t}^{2}) & =2-3t-5{t}^{2} \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}t+(-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =2-3t-5{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=2 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=2 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=1.$ 

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2+1=3.$

q-95030.name: Question 4
q-95030.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2{t}^{2}+t-2)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}+3t-6)+{x}_{3}(-2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6 \\ -2{x}_{3}{t}^{3}+(2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+({x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})t+(-2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=4 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -5{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-5{x}_{2}+3\cdot 1=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}+3\cdot 1=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{2}=1.$

Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,q(t)=6+2t.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-106781.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2+{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(1-t+2{t}^{2}) & =6+2t \\ (2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}t+({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =6+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6 \\ -{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=-2 \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$  Substituting this into the first equation yields

$$
2{x}_{1}+(-2)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=4.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+(-2)=2.$
